highlights.title: Anthropic AI Model Went Rogue, Submitted Fake Tip to Police
highlights.description: Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model carried out additional unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations, including submitting a false tip in a police homicide case, prompting a warning from the Trump administration for artificial intelligence companies to secure their systems.

highlights.title: Anthropic can’t reliably control its AI agents. It’s cutting off its internal evals from the live internet instead
highlights.description: Anthropic said it "turned off live internet access" for "all our internal evaluations" until further notice.

highlights.description:
Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 147, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you're new here, welcome, I missed you all, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.)

highlights.description:

highlights.title: Nvidia GPUs are everywhere. Here are the ways companies are accessing them

highlights.title: Nvidia reportedly halts GeForce RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs
highlights.description: Nvidia reportedly discontinues GeForce RTX 5090-series products leaving GB202 for data center and professional graphics boards. GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB rumored to become de-facto flagship from the green camp for a while.

highlights.title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving is now called Assisted Driving in Europe
highlights.description: Tesla has renamed Full Self-Driving in Europe, as it seeks to get it approved in more countries.

highlights.title: Turkey Bans Social Media Accounts for Children Under 15
highlights.description: Turkey has barred social media platforms from providing services to children under the age of 15, according to a regulation published in the Official Gazette.

ev_autonomous.title: The Telo MT1 is a big truck trapped in a tiny truck’s body
ev_autonomous.description:
I'm bouncing down the road in San Carlos, California, zipping past behemoth tech companies like EA and Oracle, in America's smallest electric truck.
The Telo MT1 (which stands for "mini truck") unquestionably turns heads because it looks so remarkably different from everything else on the market right now. 
It has a nearly cab-over design, meaning that front-seat passengers sit almost directly over the front axle. It looks a lot like a Japanese kei truck, with a super-short nose and four doors. People stop to stare as we sit at stoplights or roll silently past.
